title: Viking Realms: six months building a Norse free-to-play game with Claude Code and Codex
author: Admirable-Earth-5041
selftext:
I’ve had the idea for Viking Realms for about two years. The initial commit has been sitting there since early 2025. Six months ago I started building it properly, with two AI tools doing most of the work.

You found a holding on a map of the North Sea, grow it into a settlement, scout your neighbours, form alliances and besiege rivals, all in a persistent world shared with other players. Combat is stat-based, closer to Crusader Kings than an RTS.

**How the work split.** Claude Code (Opus 5.5) does the engineering: the Three.js client, the Laravel backend, and the server-side rules for anything that affects another player. Codex (6.1 Sol) does most of the visual work: badges, avatars, portraits and icons. It consistently gave better first drafts for anything that has to look like art rather than UI.

https://reddit.com/link/1xzvbsw/video/cmxj1sukpg2i1/player

**The rules file.** The biggest win wasn’t either model. It was a file of standing rules both tools read before every change: “could a cheater exploit this?”, gold buys cosmetics only, everything fits the Viking age (no potatoes, though pumpkins got a pass for Halloween, because reasons), and names stay plain. Anything I had to correct twice became a rule.

**Where it went wrong.** This evening my town vanished from my dev save. I spent a while digging into it with the AI, but what saved the evening was the backups: I could restore everything and carry on. If you’re building with AI, set those up early. It’ll happily build features all day, but it won’t suggest the boring safety nets unless you ask.

**My part.** I’ve been a software engineer for 15 years. These days I mostly play the game and tell the AI what I want in it.

It’s in early access at playvikingrealms.com. I’ll be in the comments if you want to ask about the workflow or how the two tools compare.
